content_text: Ten years ago, a tragedy forever changed the lives of our Woodmore Elementary School families and the Hamilton County community. Today, we pause to remember and honor the six precious children whose lives were lost and the 31 children whose lives were forever changed that afternoon. A decade has passed, but the memory of these children and the impact they had on our community remains. We hold their families, friends, classmates, educators, and all those impacted by this tragedy close in our hearts. As a Hamilton County Schools community, we remain committed to honoring their memories and surrounding those who continue to carry the weight of that day with love, compassion, and support.
A decade has passed since the Woodmore bus crash cut innocent lives short. We remember the victims on this anniversary and the dedication of the first responders who worked this tragic call. ✝️ 🕊️

Department: Public Works- Engineering Division CLASSIFICATION SUMMARY: Incumbents in this classification are responsible for performing supervisory and technical work associated with overseeing the City's stormwater construction sites program and ensuring right-of-way compliance. Responsibilities include drainage design activities; right-of-way compliance reviews; and field inspection of drainage problems and construction activities to control and reduce the discharge of pollutants and sediments during construction projects. Work requires limited supervision and the use of independent judgment and discretion. SERIES LEVEL: The Construction Program Manager is a stand-alone position. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: (The following duties ARE NOT intended to serve as a comprehensive list of all duties performed by all employees in this classification, only a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties.) Supervises staff to include prioritizing and assigning work; conducting performance evaluations; ensuring staff is trained; ensuring that employees follow policies and procedures; maintaining a healthy and safe working environment; and making hiring, termination, and disciplinary recommendations. Supervises day-to-day project activities related to the City's stormwater construction sites and right-of-way programs, which includes planning, coordinating, administering, and evaluating programs, projects, processes, procedures, systems, standards, and/or service offerings; ensures compliance with federal, state, and local laws, right-of-way regulations, codes, and/or standards. Reviews, prepares, analyzes, and prioritizes work orders and design changes in order to eliminate engineering, right-of-way, and stormwater drainage problems. Serves as a liaison between internal departments, the City Council, elected officials, property owners, external agencies, developers, and/or other interested parties regarding stormwater and right-of-way matters. Partners with land agents, internal divisions, property owners, and outside agencies on project permits and land acquisitions; aligns work operations, monitors project progress, shares information, and resolves operational issues. Responds to citizen calls, complaints, and inquiries regarding engineering, drainage, and right-of-way issues—including unauthorized encroachments, sight-distance obstructions, drainage interference, and unpermitted work within the public right-of-way; conducts related field investigations to assess compliance and property impacts; and performs necessary follow-up activities to achieve resolution. Conducts inspections of construction projects to ensure compliance with applicable construction plans and codes. Supervises and monitors construction activities to control and reduce the discharge of pollutants and sediment from project sites. Oversees construction operations to ensure all development and land disturbance within City rights-of-way adhere strictly to federal, state, and local codes, regulations, and guidelines. Reviews and participates in the preparation and analysis of a variety of data and information; formulates recommendations based on findings; manages priorities, work processes, and procedures; ensures adherence and compatibility with organizational goals, objectives, and strategic initiatives. Researches deeds, plat books, subdivision plats, and surveys to identify ownership and property lines. Prepares legal descriptions for the purchase of right-of-way or easements for projects. Designs engineering and drainage projects. Reviews and performs computer-aided design and manual preparation of construction plans and designs. Represents the department and/or the City at a variety of meetings, public events, training sessions, committees, and/or other related events or groups in order to receive and convey information pertaining to City policy, projects, or programs. Manages and administers a variety of contracts and associated activities, which include compiling and publishing contract documents and specifications for bids. Directs and manages drainage contracts; represents the department in pre-bid meetings, bid openings, and pre-construction meetings; attends final inspections when engineering/drainage contract projects are completed, and performs other related activities. Responsible for reading current technical literature, maintaining professional affiliations, and attending workshops and technical training sessions when appropriate. Must meet regular attendance requirements. Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers, and citizens. Must accomplish the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodations, in a timely manner. Performs other duties as assigned. Level I (Fundamentals of Erosion Prevention Sediment Control) required. Must be able to obtain a Special Police Commission badge within 6 months of hire. T.D.E.C. Level II (Design Principles of Erosion Prevention Sediment Controls for Construction Sites) preferred. Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC) or Certified Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System Specialist (CMS4S) preferred. Additional requirements for Transportation Right of Way work unit: TDOT Hot Mix Asphalt Roadway Inspector ATSSA Temporary Traffic Control Plans Certification within one (1) year of hire. Skill in monitoring and evaluating the work of subordinate staff; prioritizing and assigning work; designing stormwater projects; managing and administering contracts; using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems; identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions; interpreting and applying applicable laws, ordinances, codes, rules, regulations, standards, policies and procedures; providing public relations; coordinating, scheduling and prioritizing activities with applicable interested parties and communication and interpersonal skills as applied to interaction with coworkers, supervisor, and the general public, sufficient to exchange or convey information and to receive work direction. The Mental Health Specialist works under the direction of the Disability Mental Health Coordinator to promote children's social-emotional well-being, positive behavior, emotional regulation, and successful participation in classroom activities. The position collaborates with families, educators, program staff, consultants, and community partners to identify concerns, coordinate services, implement appropriate supports, and monitor children's progress. Mental health is the primary focus of the position; however, cross-coverage for Disability Specialist functions is a required secondary responsibility based on staffing and program needs. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: The following duties are NOT intended to serve as a comprehensive list of all duties performed by all employees in this classification, only a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Primary Responsibilities – Mental Health Services Observe and assess children's social-emotional development and behavioral needs, assisting with the development and implementation of individualized behavior support strategies. Provide classroom-based behavioral support, including modeling appropriate strategies, assisting with de-escalation, and coaching educators in positive behavior management practices. Collaborate with families, educators, consultants, and program staff to address behavioral concerns, coordinate interventions, and connect families with appropriate resources. Monitor children's progress, evaluate the effectiveness of behavioral supports, and maintain accurate and confidential documentation. Assist with social-emotional screenings, staff training, mental health consultation, and other program initiatives that promote children's social-emotional well-being. Maintain assigned site visits, meetings, records, and follow-up activities in accordance with program expectations. Support compliance with applicable Head Start Program Performance Standards, program policies, procedures, and documentation requirements. Complete other related duties as assigned. Cross-Coverage Responsibilities – Disability Services Receive cross-training and provide Disability Specialist coverage as directed by the Disability Mental Health Coordinator to maintain continuity of services. Assist with developmental screenings, identification of potential developmental concerns, referrals, and coordination of services for children with suspected or identified disabilities. Support the coordination and monitoring of Individualized Family Service Plans (IFSPs), Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), and related services, including communication with families, educators, and community partners. Provide classroom guidance and support related to accommodations, modifications, and strategies that promote the inclusion and participation of children with disabilities. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor's Degree in Early Childhood Development, Special Education, Applied Behavior Analysis, Psychology, Social Work, Human Services, or similar content area. A minimum of two (2) years of experience working with children ages eight weeks through five years. Any combination of equivalent experience and education to perform the essential functions of the position will be considered. LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS: Relevant credentials or certifications—such as Registered Behavior Technician (RBT), Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst (BCaBA), Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), social work, early childhood, special education, or other related credentials—are preferred when applicable. CLASS certification is required if designated by the program. KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS: Knowledge of: Knowledge of early childhood social-emotional development, positive behavior supports, and developmentally appropriate practice. Ability to observe and document children’s behavior objectively and maintain accurate records. Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with families, educators, program staff, consultants, and community partners. Ability to model strategies and provide respectful, practical coaching to classroom staff. Ability to manage assigned responsibilities, respond to changing program needs, and provide cross-coverage as directed. Ability to maintain confidentiality and follow applicable program policies and procedures. Skills in: Communication Computer Systems (i.e. Microsoft and Google Suites) Classroom Modifications Advocacy Behavior Management De-escalation Techniques Identifying Disabilities PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Positions in this class typically require: walking, standing, reaching, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions. It takes split-second coordination and immense courage to pull someone from a burning vehicle—and on the night of November 6, 2026, Squad 13 Green Shift crew delivered when it mattered most. Responding to a crash on I-24 Eastbound, S13 arrived to find a pickup truck on fire against the barrier with the driver trapped inside. Captain Richard Pershey, Lt. Matthew Doss, Senior Firefighter Charles Simpson, Firefighter Kenneth Coffee, and Firefighter Barrett Rozzell worked together to tackle the fire and free the injured driver from the burning truck. They were assisted by Franklin Fire Lt.-Paramedic Austin Cooper who was off-duty at the time and traveling through Chattanooga when he spotted the wreck. Today, we presented Squad 13 Green Shift with Life-Saving Awards in recognition of their decisive actions and dedication to protecting our community. We also extend our deepest gratitude to these firefighters, including Lt. Cooper, for stepping up to help in a critical moment and saving someone’s life. Job well done!

CPD Arrests Two People In Roanoke Ave Homicide CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) has arrested two people in connection to a homicide on Roanoke Avenue. At approximately 8:30 a.m. on November 17, 2026 officers responded to reports of a deceased person in the 1800 block of Roanoke Avenue. Upon arrival, officers located a 24-year-old man with multiple gunshot wounds. He was pronounced dead at the scene. CPD's Crime Scene and Homicide Units responded to process and investigate the scene. The preliminary investigation indicates the suspect, Qence Burgess (DOB: 12/12/2002), was dropped off, waited for the victim, and shot him. During an interview, Burgess confessed to the shooting. He is charged with First Degree Murder and Tampering with Evidence. A second suspect, Jessica Williams (DOB: 2/10/1982), is charged with Facilitation of First Degree Murder. Both suspects were transported to the Hamilton County Jail.  This remains an active and ongoing investigation. This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. The Chattanooga Police Department asks anyone with information about this incident to call (423) 698-2525. The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct and not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law. #CPDnews

Find out how you can get involved to help reduce violence in Chattanooga with CURV by following their Facebook page!OUR COMMUNITIES. OUR VOICES. OUR COMMITMENT. In light of the recent gun violence impacting our community, we want to extend our sincere gratitude to everyone who came out and stood with us in solidarity. We especially want to recognize our 423 Chainbreakers for their leadership in organizing these efforts and bringing our community together in a show of unity and support. On Monday, we gathered in the Alton Park community, and yesterday, we stood together along Roanoke Avenue, holding signs and raising our voices in a united message: ENOUGH IS ENOUGH. We also want to thank Councilwoman Roquetta Dotley and Hamilton County Commissioner Montrell Besley, who joined us Monday in Alton Park, and Councilwoman Marvene Noel, who joined us Tuesday on Roanoke Avenue. We appreciate their willingness to stand alongside our residents and demonstrate their commitment to safer neighborhoods. Their presence and support matter. Paul Feaster regularly visits the Hixson Community Center to enjoy pickleball and connect with fellow residents. With more than 40 years of experience as a paramedic, Paul understands how critical it is to have the right equipment available during a medical emergency. During a competitive game of pickleball, he recognized that the center's existing first-aid resources were not sufficient to provide potentially life-saving assistance while waiting for emergency responders to arrive. Rather than simply raising a concern, Paul took action. He met with Hixson Community Center Manager Kevin McGowan and spoke with City Council members to advocate for accessible Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) in community centers. His advocacy sparked an important conversation and became a priority for the Department of Community Development. As a result of Paul's call to action, the department made it a mission to ensure AEDs were installed and accessible in every Chattanooga community center, helping create safer spaces for the residents who visit them every day. Hear Paul's story and learn how one resident's initiative helped move the needle to make a life-saving difference across our community.

📜 Thank you, Hamilton County! 💗 Hamilton County Mayor Weston Wamp has officially proclaimed November 2026 as Family Court Awareness Month for the fifth year! We are grateful to Mayor Wamp for recognizing that children’s safety must be the central consideration in our family courts, especially in cases involving abuse or violence. Why does this matter? Family courts make life-changing decisions about divorce, custody, visitation, dependency and neglect, and domestic violence. Wear pink in recognition of the children whose safety and well-being are affected by family court proceedings, and to remember those we’ve lost.  Share your photo and tag us! HAPPY BIRTHDAY, CFD: The Chattanooga Fire Department marks 155 years of continuous service today, celebrating a legacy that began in the ashes of the post-Civil War era and evolved into one of Tennessee’s premier modern emergency response organizations. Prior to 1871, fire protection in Chattanooga relied on loosely organized volunteer bucket brigades and early hand-drawn pumpers. As the city rapidly transformed into a major railroad and industrial hub following the Civil War, timber-framed buildings, crowded rail yards, and expanding manufacturing plants created fire hazards that outpaced volunteer capacity. On November 14, 1871, the Chattanooga Fire Department (CFD) was formed. City leaders formally established a paid department, commissioning Engine Company No. 1. Equipped with steam-powered fire engines pulled by teams of trained fire horses, the fledgling department laid the foundation for organized, full-time municipal fire protection in the Scenic City. Over the years, the department grew alongside Chattanooga’s booming population and industrial footprint. Today, at 155 years strong, the Chattanooga Fire Department operates with more than 400 sworn personnel working out of twenty stations across the city. The CFD functions as an all-hazards emergency response agency, providing advanced fire suppression & rescue, specialized technical rescue, emergency medical response, and fire prevention & community risk reduction.  Across 155 years, the tools have changed—from leather buckets and steam boilers to thermal imaging cameras, aerial ladders, and specialized rescue equipment—but the core mission has remained constant. Generations of Chattanooga firefighters have answered the call with courage, professionalism, and an unwavering commitment to protecting lives and property across the Scenic City. We pay tribute to all of our firefighters- past and present- as we continue to pave the way for the future.

As Executive Director of the Family Justice Center, I have the great honor of working alongside an incredibly talented and dedicated team of staff, partners, and supporters who pour their hearts into making a difference in our community. ❤️ The past few weeks have been a whirlwind, but they’ve reminded me just how blessed I am to do this work with such amazing people! From Washington, D.C., to international conversations and celebrating the talent in our own backyard, these past few weeks have reinforced something I deeply believe: relationships matter, collaboration makes us stronger, and amazing things happen when people come together for their community. And while I’ve had the privilege of representing the FJC at these events, our incredible staff continues the important work every single day, walking alongside survivors, educating our community, and coordinating responses that strengthen victim safety and offender accountability. I couldn’t be prouder or more grateful for this team’s dedication, compassion, and commitment! I’m so thankful for the friendships, partnerships, and opportunities this work brings, but most of all, for the amazing people I get to share this journey with. Department: WW - Solid Waste Handling SERIES LEVEL: The Plant Operator 2 is the second level of a four-level wastewater plant operations series. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: (The following duties ARE NOT intended to serve as a comprehensive list of all duties performed by all employees in this classification, only a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties.) Maintains, operates, and checks the operation of all collection systems, lift stations, and chlorination facilities; operates pumps, valves, and other equipment by hand or mechanical means to regulate the flow of wastewater through various primary and secondary treatment processes; maintains an even flow to assure maximum efficiency of plant equipment and compliance with regulatory requirements. Operates multiple pump stations, which include station maintenance, emergency repair, and response; data collection, record-keeping, and sample collection. Collects samples of wastewater and other materials at scheduled times; performs standardized control tests; operates, adjusts, and maintains chemical feed equipment to ensure compliance with established standards; performs record-keeping functions such as logging plant operations, test results, maintenance work, and unusual operating conditions encountered; prepares special reports as required. Reads and monitors meters, gauges, charts, instruments, and computerized systems to identify potential problems and ensure continuous operations; changes recording charts and ensures their continuous operation. Performs routine and higher-level maintenance at plant facilities and grounds, including washing down the facility daily, maintaining grounds such as cutting grass and light maintenance duties, the sludge handling facilities including odor control and performing general housekeeping duties; performs maintenance of plant machinery, equipment, piping, and structures; cleans air diffusers, clears blockages from pipes and valves, and performs repairs as necessary. Prepares and records a variety of readings and information related to plant operations in applicable logbooks. May ensure that all daily samples, Chains-of-Custody, and Daily Reports correctly follow the State and Federal regulations before preparing and disseminating a variety of routine and legally mandated reports related to wastewater plant operations. Routine duties involve highly skilled work of operating, maintaining, and monitoring wastewater (sludge) flows and stabilization in the treatment plant. Specifically in solids, it involves the operation of high-volume, high-speed centrifuges in order to recycle the sludge into usable organic fertilizer. Utilize computerized graphic displays for Centrifuges, conveyors, pumps, plus controlled chemical mixing and injection; then verify and interpret the process and direct proper personnel to resolve any problems, ensuring efficient and safe plant operations. May perform skilled technical work in the operation of the Moccasin Bend Wastewater Treatment Plant, utilizing a bank of four computer monitors, monitoring all 88 pump stations and CSO’s from a secure location. May observe, maintain, and provide Situational awareness to remote facilities operations via SCADA in order to control equipment, conditions, and personnel during a 12-hour rotating shift. Coordinate operational failures with the maintenance and Electrical departments or other agencies as required. May coordinate with other departments, vendors, and Contractors for access to secure work sites. May maintain contact via Radio/ phone communication with outside workers and contractors. May conduct site visits after normal work hours as needed in case of loss of communication, station failure, or unforeseen problems as they arise. If unable to troubleshoot/ repair problems in a timely manner, contact the on-call operator, mechanic, or electrician as needed. May operate a City vehicle to carry out duties at pump stations throughout the city. Must meet regular attendance requirements. Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers, and citizens. Must accomplish the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodations, in a timely manner. Performs other duties as assigned. This position is deemed essential during inclement weather situations and must report to or remain at work, even when administrative closings are announced, as determined by the Department Head. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: High School Diploma or GED supplemented by vocational/technical training in wastewater treatment plant operations' or a related field and six (6) months of work experience in a wastewater treatment plant, operating chemical processing equipment, clarifiers, collecting and lab testing samples, sludge inventory, adjusting flows and/or reading meters; or any equivalent combination of education, training/experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job. OR High School diploma or GED with six (6) months of water or wastewater operations experience and a Grade II Moccasin Bend Environmental Campus Wastewater Certification. This is a career ladder position. This position will receive an automatic progression to Plant Operator 3 when the incumbent has achieved the required minimum qualifications and licenses/certifications for the next position in the series. LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS: Valid Driver’s License KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS: Knowledge of operation, maintenance and repair of wastewater plant equipment and facilities; wastewater treatment principles, methods and practices; operation and maintenance of a wide variety of tools and equipment utilized in the trade; mathematical concepts; safety rules, codes and regulations and safe work methods and precautions related to the work; methods and precautions in storing and handling chlorine and other hazardous gasses and chemicals; routine process control tests; and preventative maintenance practices and procedures as applied to wastewater treatment facilities and collection systems. Skill in operating wastewater treatment plant equipment; performing routine maintenance and making operating adjustments to wastewater equipment; cleaning facilities and equipment; recognizing unusual, inefficient or dangerous operating conditions and taking appropriate action; reading and recording data from gauges and meters; performing routine control tests and adjust plant equipment accordingly; preparing and maintaining a variety of records and logs of work performed; and communication and interpersonal skills as applied to interaction with coworkers, supervisor, and the general public, sufficient to exchange or convey information and to receive work direction. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Positions in this class typically require climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, and seeing. WORK ENVIRONMENT: Medium Work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Incumbents may be subjected to moving mechanical parts, electrical currents, vibrations, fumes, odors, dusts, gases, poor ventilation, chemicals, oils, extreme temperatures, inadequate lighting, work space restrictions, intense noises, and travel. Chattanooga Police Department Retires K9 Baba CHATTANOOGA, Tenn.  –  After years of dedicated service, the Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) announces the retirement of K9 Baba, a decorated explosives detection and patrol dog. K9 Baba, a 7-year-old German Shepherd, retired after 5 years with CPD. During her distinguished career, K9 Baba performed several hundred sweeps for explosives and located more than 30 firearms, keeping the community and visitors to the Scenic City safe.  K9 Baba worked numerous high-profile events, including the FIFA World Cup, IRONMAN 70.3 and 140.6, Moon River, and the Blue Cross Bowl. K9 Baba also enjoyed locating suspects and assisting patrol, investigative units, and federal partners. Outside of Chattanooga, K9 Baba earned recognition for her exceptional performance at competitions. Most recently, she was named "Top Dog" at the 2025 United States Police Canine Association (USPCA) Region 22 explosives trials. In 2024, K9 Baba and her handler, Officer John Isler, claimed second place in the American Tactical K9 Association Best Team Competition. The Chattanooga Police Department thanks K9 Baba for her time with the department and recognizes the commitment of her handler (Ofc Isler), his family, and community members who support the K9 Unit. The Chattanooga Police Department wishes K9 Baba a long, healthy retirement.

One of our team member, David Collins, shares his son's NYC Marathon experience. 😊 "As a proud dad, I couldn’t be more excited to share the incredible accomplishment of my 27-year-old son, Mike, who recently completed the 50th Anniversary TCS New York City Marathon! This was Mike’s third marathon, following previous finishes in the St. Jude Marathon in Memphis and the Charlotte Marathon. Running 26.2 miles through the streets of New York City is an extraordinary challenge, but being part of such a historic milestone made it even more special. What makes the accomplishment even sweeter is that Mike crossed the finish line in just over 4 hours and 30 minutes, recording his fastest marathon time yet and setting a new personal record! What many people don’t realize is that running a marathon is about much more than the 26.2 miles on race day. It takes months of preparation, discipline, and an incredible commitment to training. We’re talking countless hours of running, early mornings, long miles, and pushing through when your body is telling you otherwise. In the final weeks leading up to the race, Mike was tackling grueling 15- to 20-mile training runs a few times a month before the marathon. That’s a level of dedication and determination that is difficult to appreciate unless you’ve experienced it. As his parents, we couldn’t be prouder. Watching him set ambitious goals, put in the work, and see it all come together on one of the world’s biggest marathon stages is incredibly rewarding. At just 27 years old, Mike has already accomplished something most people would never attempt, much less complete three times. His mom and I are beyond proud of him, and we look forward to seeing what challenge he takes on next!" David Collins, Admin Manager for City Wide Services

🐾🇺🇸 PAWS OFF! PURPOSE ON! 🇺🇸🐾 A working service dog is not simply a dog wearing a vest. They are someone’s independence, safety, freedom, and sometimes even their lifeline. When you see a service dog in public, you may see an adorable face, a wagging tail, and a beautiful animal you’d love to pet. But what you may not see is the invisible disability, the countless hours of specialized training, or the life-changing tasks that dog has been trained to perform. ❤️ That service dog has a job to do, and that job matters! Service dogs assist individuals with a wide range of disabilities, including mobility limitations, neurological conditions, seizure disorders, PTSD, vision loss, and many other visible and invisible disabilities. A moment of distraction may seem harmless, but it could prevent a service dog from recognizing an important medical change, responding to an emergency, or helping their handler remain safe. 🐾 So how can YOU help? Simply respect the working partnership. Don’t pet, call, whistle at, feed, or distract a working service dog. Give the team room to navigate safely, and always speak directly to the handler rather than trying to engage the dog. And remember, not every disability is visible. Someone should never have to explain their medical history to receive kindness, dignity, and respect. As Mrs. Chattanooga America, my platform, Accessibility for All, is about more than awareness. It’s about education, advocacy, inclusion, and ensuring that individuals with disabilities have the same opportunities to participate fully in everyday life. Service dogs aren’t accessories. They aren’t entertainment. They are highly trained working partners who help make independence possible. 🇺🇸 And for our veterans who rely on service dogs, these extraordinary partnerships can mean renewed confidence, greater independence, and the freedom to reclaim parts of life they once thought were lost. Accessibility begins with awareness, but real inclusion begins with ACTION. 🐾 Here’s my challenge to you: The next time you see a working service dog, admire that beautiful partnership from a respectful distance. Your kindness may be the very thing that allows that team to do its job safely. ❤️ PLEASE SHARE THIS POST! You never know who may need this reminder. One share can educate someone, change a perspective, and help protect a working service dog team. Because accessibility isn’t a privilege. It’s a right. 👑 Mrs. Chattanooga America 2026 🐾 Accessibility for All Paws Off! Purpose On! Warrior Freedom Service DogsThe Dog Wizard Chattanooga John Hayes Mayor’s Council on Disability

Meet Ciraea Nilsen and Nakisha Jones. They are two of the many participants who recently completed the Parent Academy program offered by the Office of Community Health. Parent Academy is a free 8-week program designed to empower parents and caregivers with the tools to support their children’s academic, social, and emotional development. Both women are returning participants who came back because of the resources and support. They valued learning about options they didn’t know existed and enjoyed meeting community partners who exposed them to resources to help support their family. Ciraea's main takeaway was the number of resources she hadn’t known about. She named two in particular: life insurance and further schooling. Congratulations to Battalion Chief Travis Williams as he starts the next exciting chapter of his illustrious career in the fire service! I appreciate the opportunity to serve the citizens of Signal Mountain. I am excited to get started.” Welcome to the Mountain, Chief! May lead financial planning to ensure the short and long term fiscal health of the utility and enterprise fund. May serve as staff lead for engagement with state and federal officials regarding state and federal utility loan programs, including SRF and WIFIA. May work with consultants, and develop and oversee the annual capital budget and program. May direct and oversee the day to day activities and operations of the following utility work areas: Sewer billing; Blanket contracts, procurement, invoicing, requisitioning; Capital contracts, procurement, invoicing, and requisitioning; Division payroll functions; Warehouse services, including asset management, procurement and storage of equipment, parts, and other supplies; Budget, both operating and capital; Work Order management. May direct and manage subordinate wastewater utility staff to include: prioritizing and assigning work; conducting performance evaluations; ensuring staff are trained; ensuring that employees follow policies and procedures; maintaining a healthy and safe working environment; and, making hiring, termination, and disciplinary recommendations. Approves leave requests. May perform departmental leadership duties, including assisting with developing policies, operating procedures, rules, regulations, and work methods, and makes recommendations for their improvement. Formulates long- and short-range goals and objectives for better operating efficiency. Evaluates staff procedures on a continuous basis; recommends and implements improvements where necessary. Interprets rules, policies, and procedures for staff members. May drive and support continuous improvement activities related to safety, quality, and cost. May represent the City of Chattanooga’s interests towards suppliers and contractors. May compile and provide reports related to areas of responsibility. May cooperate and collaborate with groups and individuals across all departments and divisions, and other service units with focus on achieving optimal results/solutions. Must perform all tasks and assignments in accordance with The City of Chattanooga’s policies and procedures. Must ensure all required training is completed in a timely manner made by all team members in their area of responsibility. Must meet regular attendance requirements. Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers, and citizens. Must accomplish the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodations, in a timely manner. Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors Recreation Division officially honored local Negro League baseball trailblazers with city plaques celebrating their excellence, sportsmanship, and lasting impact on our community. This honor was part of several last Sunday as a part of tribute to historic Lincoln Park.  David Crutcher, Mr. Swafford, James Tatum, Charles White and receiving an honorary jersey, Jackie Simpson. Thank you for your dedication.  These awards do more than look back at the impact of the historic Negro League, they help us pave the way forward. Many of these honorees continue to pour into our youth throughout the community and the Chattanooga RBI Baseball and Softball Program, opening doors for hundreds of local kids to play, learn, and compete completely free of charge. Thank you Administrator David Johnson and Recreation Director Greta Hayes for the plaques and support! content_text: Grateful to present at Shared Hope International’s JuST Conference with amazing colleagues and friends, Sarah McKinnis, Christine M. Raino, and Sara Bendtsen Diedhiou, sharing the work of the Chattanooga Pilot Project! 💜 Our session, “From Conversation to Cultivation,” highlighted our collaboration to build community-based responses supporting youth impacted by human trafficking, listening to survivors, identifying gaps, and bringing local and national partners together to create a stronger safety net. Carol Berz was a driving force to initiate this coordinated effort and has impacted it evolution.  I’m proud to represent the Dr. Carol B. Berz Family Justice Center and a community willing to ask, “Can we commit together to the survivors in our community?” That shared commitment is what One Chattanooga looks like in action.
